title: Setup transaction journal
description: What setup was doing when it stopped, and what would resume it. ⚠️ IT EXISTS ONLY WHILE SETUP IS INCOMPLETE. Written before the first lasting write and REMOVED on success, so its presence is itself the signal that a run was interrupted — a journal that lingered after a clean run would make every subsequent start look like a recovery. ⚠️ IT RECORDS FILE IDENTITIES, NEVER FILE CONTENTS (section 13). The transaction re-reads and compares identities under the lock so a concurrent edit refuses rather than being overwritten; storing the content instead would put a copy of the operator's settings — and whatever they had put in them — into an ignored file nobody audits. ⚠️ AND NEVER A CONFIG VALUE: the point of the journal is which phase completed, not what it configured.

operation.description: Which invocation opened this journal. ⚠️ A resume that is itself interrupted must not read as a fresh setup, because the recovery advice differs.

phases.description: The ordered plan, with each phase's outcome. ⚠️ THE WHOLE PLAN IS WRITTEN UP FRONT, not appended as it goes: a journal that only lists what has happened cannot say what was supposed to happen next, which is the one thing a recovery needs.

status.description: ⚠️ `running` IS A REAL PERSISTED STATE. A process killed mid-phase leaves exactly one, and that is what distinguishes 'this phase never started' from 'this phase may have half-happened' — which decides whether recovery can simply rerun it.

detail.description: A non-secret note about the outcome. Never a credential, a variable value, or an absolute path.

lastCompletedPhase.description: Named rather than indexed, so inserting a phase in a later version does not silently reinterpret an old journal as having got further than it did.

fileIdentities.description: The identity of each file the transaction may merge, recorded before the plan is applied and re-compared under the lock immediately before each merge.

root.description: Which authorized root `path` is relative to. ⚠️ REQUIRED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because the two roots are not always nested: with `--local-state user` the state root lives under `%LOCALAPPDATA%` or `$XDG_STATE_HOME`, outside the project entirely. A bare relative path would then be ambiguous — and resolving it against the wrong root is how a recovery compares a file against an identity recorded for a different file. ⚠️ Naming the root is also what keeps the ABSOLUTE path out of this record: REQ-0024 forbids a user-home path in anything Kiln writes, and the external state root is exactly one.

state.description: ⚠️ `absent` IS RECORDED, not omitted. 'This file did not exist when I planned' and 'I did not look at this file' lead to different actions, and an omitted entry cannot tell them apart — a file that appeared between plan and merge must refuse, not merge.

digest.description: Present exactly when `state` is `present`. Over the file's bytes — never over anything credential-bearing.

recovery.description: How to continue. ⚠️ AN EXACT COMMAND, not a description of one: an operator recovering from an interrupted setup is the least well-placed person to reconstruct the invocation, and a paraphrase is how a recovery becomes a second incident.

allOf.$comment: A present file must carry a digest and an absent one must not — the pairing is what makes the comparison meaningful rather than a matter of remembering to fill it in.
